data.gender_notes: Yamini is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of the Night, Darkness, or Death
data.long_meaning: Yamini is a name of the Goddess of Death, Yama's consort, who is believed to take the souls of the deceased to the underworld. She is also known as the Goddess of the Night or Darkness. In some Hindu mythologies, she is also considered a goddess of joy and happiness. The name Yamini carries the meaning “Goddess of the Night, Darkness, or Death” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Yamini usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the night, darkness, or death and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Yamini is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life and death. She represents the power of transformation and the idea that even in death, there is joy and happiness to be found.
data.etymology: Yamini belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Night, Darkness, or Death.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yamini total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Yamini was the name of the wife of the god of death, Yama, in Hindu mythology. She is often depicted as the goddess of death, darkness, and the night. She is also known as Yami or Yamanika.

According to the Mahabharata, Yamini was the daughter of the demon king Daruka and the goddess Hema. She was married to Yama, the god of death, and is often referred to as Yama's queen. She is said to have helped Yama in his duties as the god of death, and is sometimes depicted as a benevolent and merciful figure.
